name: Argonaut mine (Georgetown)
quote: Later, in 1927, it was again the subject of a promotion, and 60 tons of low-grade rock was milled. In 1928, a small tonnage of rock yielded about $15 a ton.

name: Big Four claim
quote: Forty tons of ore was reported to have yielded $10 a ton in free gold, and another lot of 50 tons produced $13 a ton, not including sulphides, regarding the amount and value of which nothing is known.

name: Church mine (El Dorado or Church Union)
quote: In July, 1890, the ore is stated to have averaged $8 to $9 a ton in the 10-stamp mill in August, $13 and in September, better than that, exclusive of sulphides.

name: Church Union mine (above 1,300-foot level)
quote: The ore milled dovm. as far as the 1300-ft. level had averaged $17 a ton.

name: Chaparral (Golden Queen) claim
quote: From then until 1875 the property had a mill and was a small producer of ore reported to have yielded from $7 to $15 a ton.

name: Cincinnati mine
quote: In 1917 the claim was equipped with a light 5-stamp mill and the first clean-up early in 1918 is reported to have given an average return of $3.82 a ton by amalgamation alone.

name: Coe Hill mine (Gold Star or Bathurst)
quote: Late in 1921, A. Tetrault and associates milled 50 tons from a dump and from an adit, which is reported to have plated $7 a ton.

name: Crown Point and Gold Queen Consolidated
quote: Here the ore was reported in small lenses. Several small lots are said to have jdelded $20 a ton or more.

name: Dalmatia (Kelly) mine
quote: The property before that had been known as the Kelly mine and a shaft had been sunk 260 ft. upon a vein two feet wide, crossing the main seam belt lode at an acute angle and producing ore which is said to have yielded $16 a ton.

name: Golden Gate (McNulty or Oakland) mine
quote: According to James Richards, who was formerly engineer of the property, this ore averaged $15 a ton in a 10-stamp mill then located on the mine.

name: Gopher-Boulder mine (Gopher workings)
quote: Ore was mined in two open pits and dropped through raises to a lower adit. Ore averaged $2.50 a ton and made in flat quartz stringers making into the main lode with a low dip to east.

name: Gopher-Boulder mine (Boulder vein)
quote: The ore shoot was followed 130 ft. north and 120 ft. south from the shaft and was mined 7 ft. wide. Old records indicate it paid $6 a ton in free gold and show a production of $40,000 from it.

name: Griffith Consolidated (700-foot level mill test)
quote: by the company to mine 2000 tons of ore and mill tests of this ore, according to the former superintendent, went $4.25 on the plates and 3% sulphides worth $42 a ton.

name: Griffith Consolidated (Klondike workings, 100-ton lot)
quote: Two or three lots of ore from these workings milled from $20 to $65 a ton. A lot of about 100 tons taken out in 1903 is reported to have yielded $32 a ton, but there is no written record of this.

name: Harmon Group (Van Hooker claim)
quote: The ore that had been milled up to that time had yielded $7.25 to $27 a ton. Production began in 1928, and continued for three years.

name: Havilah (Nashville) mine
quote: Joshua Hendy obtained a patent in 1880 and by 1882 had sunk the shaft to a depth of 642 ft., the ore from the last 100 ft. of shaft being reported as yielding an average of $8.50 a ton.

name: Havilah (Nashville) mine (1904 run)
quote: The only production figures at hand for this period were for 1904, when the shaft was 1000 ft. deep, and when 4000 tons yielded $15,325.

name: Hines-Gilbert mine
anchor_hint: Spanish Dry Diggings, El Dorado Co.
quote: The output since 1921, less than 2000 tons in all, has varied from $3 to $40 a ton recovered.

name: Ida Livingstone claim
quote: An ore shoot 50 ft. long on top tapered to a length of 10 ft. and thickness of only six inches at the bottom. It paid $26 a ton in a custom mill.

name: Montezuma mine
quote: This company crushed over 3000 tons of ore which yielded about $8 a ton, with tailing carrying $1 to $2 a ton.

name: Montezuma mine (1,200-foot level gouge)
quote: The gouge is said to carry about 0.1 oz. of gold along the ore body.

name: Pacific mine (Placerville)
quote: Professor Thomas Price stated the ore milled from $6 to $18 a ton with a tailing loss up to 75 cents a ton.

name: Pocahontas mine
quote: The mine was then yielding ore averaging $15 a ton from a vein 4 ft. wide, and had repaid all expenses of opening and equipment.

name: River Hill mine
quote: The River Hill was an important producer from 1901 to 1906 inclusive, yielding from $2.50 to $4.80 a ton.

name: Sherman mine
quote: The total production during that period was about $136,000. The yield per ton varied from $3.15 to $6.50 and average width of vein was reported to be 5 ft., with two ore shoots 60 ft. long, between walls of Mariposa slate.

name: Sliger mine
quote: Recovery was said to be about 80%. Ore value ranged from $5 to $15 a ton. Seven men employed were producing and milling 18 tons of ore in two shifts.

name: Sliger mine (600-foot level, 1932 estimate)
quote: He believed over 100,000 tons of good ore was reasonably assured, of an average grade of about $10 a ton.

name: St. Lawrence mine
quote: For the year 1873 this company's reports showed 8062 tons milled: bullion p^roduced, $141,002.13; average per ton, $17.49.

name: St. Lawrence mine (lens below eighth level)
quote: The small lens of ore below the eighth level is claimed to have paid $27 per ton and to have yielded about $18,000.

name: Superior (Tin Cup) mine
quote: The yield of ore varied from $5.80 to $15 a ton, and concentrate worth $130 a ton made up 5% of ore.

name: Taylor (Idlewild) mine
quote: In 1890, 10 more stamps Avere added, and the 500-ft. level was opened and was producing 20 tons of ore a day, which averaged $6 a ton.

name: Taylor (Idlewild) mine (Kendall statement)
quote: This, however, is at wide variance with the statement of E. J. Kendall who said ore averaged $8.40 to $8.55 a ton.

name: Union (Springfield) mine
quote: A pay shoot north of the Union shaft is said to have yielded $450,000 from 15,000 tons of ore mined before 1868.

name: Union (Springfield) mine (1897-1909)
quote: These indicate that from 20,000 to 40,000 tons of ore was crushed annually, yielding from $5 to $7 a ton.

name: Cedarberg mine (discovery pocket)
quote: The partners mined out here 90 cubic yards which yielded $45,000 to a depth of 25 ft.

name: Cranes Gulch or Whitesides mine
quote: The Cranes Gulch or Whitesides mine had produced $100,000 from a pit 150 ft. wide by 250 ft. long by 70 ft. deep before 1874. This would indicate an average yield of over one dollar per cubic yard.

name: Argonaut mine (1913-1926 average)
quote: The paper average of $8.42 a ton for the Argonaut between 1913 and 1926 on a total of nearly a million tons conceals variations of several dollars a ton.

name: Bunker Hill mine (1899-1922)
quote: During this period, 887,585 tons of ore yielded $3,834,550. The last production amounted to $5,446 in 1925. This gives a grand total of $5,154,382.

name: Bunker Hill mine (170-270-foot levels)
quote: The ore in the upper workings was often rich, as between the 170-ft. and 270-ft. levels, where it is said to have yielded $50 to $75 a ton.

name: Central Eureka mine (east-vein shoot)
quote: The exact tonnage from this shoot is unknown but was probably about 300,000 tons which was worked with results noted (ante) between 1896 and 1907, averaging $7.16 a ton up to 1905.

name: Central Eureka mine (4,550-foot level)
quote: This level yielded over 100,000 tons of ore, carrying $10 to $14 a ton. A width of 25 ft. was stoped in places.

name: Loyal Lode claim
quote: Work was resumed in the 1880 's and in 1886 it was producing ore that yielded $7 to $8 a ton in free gold.

name: Gover mine
quote: The only figures available indicate an annual output of from $50,000 to $70,000 in the late 1880 's and early 1890 's, with the last reported production in 1894. In 1888, ore yielded $9 to $13 a ton.

name: Fremont and Gover mines (1900-1925)
quote: Between 1900 and 1925, there was a reported output of about 930,000 tons which is said to have averaged about $4 a ton recovered in the later years of work by Fremont Consolidated Mines Company the mill-heads averaged between $5 and $6 a ton.

name: Hardenberg mine
quote: Work stopped in 1895 at a depth of 1000 ft. The last ore milled in 1895 averaged $4.19 a ton.

name: Hardenberg mine (1913-1914)
quote: 1913 and 1914 reported production of 26,478 tons which yielded $65,970 or $2.49 a ton, principal!}^ from the 850-ft. and 1000-ft. levels.

name: Kennedy mine (1871-1873)
quote: In 1871 the first hoist and a 20-stamp mill were erected. From then until November, 1873, the production was $183,427 from ore of an estimated average yield of $16.67 a ton.

name: Kennedy mine (1904-1916)
quote: Sometimes high-grade quartz was struck, but yearly average mill returns were reported to be $4 to $5 a ton.

name: Kennedy mine (later selective mining)
quote: With increasing depth (4050 ft. vertically in 1920 and over 5000 ft. by 1932) and increasing cost, it has in late years been necessary to mine more selectively, with a resultant decrease in tonnage milled, and an increase in gold content of ore to one-third or two-fifths of an ounce per ton.

name: Spring Hill mine
quote: They lost it in 1854, and the new owners in 1855 produced 2221 tons of ore which yielded $21 a ton at an operating cost of $10.50 a ton.

name: South Spring Hill mine
quote: There are no figures of tonnage available, but the ore was stated in 1887 to vary in gold content from $3 to $40 a ton and in width from 1 ft. to 50 ft.

name: Keystone mine (to 1867)
quote: By 1867, a total of 44,000 tons had been worked, giving an average yield of $16 a ton or $700,000 in all.

name: Keystone mine (1927 estimate)
quote: The owners estimated in 1927 that there was 200,000 tons of proved ore that would yield $3 a ton at the old price of gold.

name: Wildman mine (1,400-foot level face)
quote: This latter width was sampled in sections of 5 ft. each, and the resulting average of the 20 samples was reported to be $3.62 a ton.

name: Old Eureka mine (Amador Consolidated)
quote: Hayward, always secretive, refused to give details of production, but local report placed the output at $6,000,000 up to 1867. In 1866 it was said 30,000 tons had yielded $27 a ton at a working cost of $5 a ton.

name: Original Amador mine (1909-1915)
quote: The ore crushed during this period came largely from development work and averaged $3.44 a ton with a reported average operating cost of $2.56 a ton.

name: Plymouth Consolidated (Empire-Phoenix ore-shoot)
quote: The vein was reported averaging 30 ft. wide and containing 1^% of concentrate worth $135 a ton. The average value of this ore was $6 to $8 a ton.

name: Plymouth Consolidated (ore-shoot below 3,400-foot level)
quote: From the 3400-ft. level about 380 ft. north of the shaft, a winze was sunk and in 1922 struck ore which developed a stope length of about 100 ft. to 180 ft. and a thickness up to 9 ft. Some 20,000 tons of ore mined from this ore-shoot averaged $10 a ton.

name: Seaton (Peerless) mine
quote: Previous to 1868, the Seaton had been opened to a depth of 500 ft. and it was stated had produced 10,000 tons of ore that yielded $9 a ton.

name: Oneida mine (1867-1868 averages)
quote: The ore on the hanging-wall side was the best, yielding $30 to $40 a ton, according to J. Ross Browne.^ The average yield in 1867 was $22 a ton and in 1868 it was $16 a ton.

name: Zeila mine
quote: There was a 16-stamp mill in 1867 and the ore at that time was said to be yielding $13.50 a ton, of which $6 a ton was said to be in free gold.

name: Zeila mine (later years)
quote: The output was about $5,000,000 for the 34 years ended in 1914, and in the later years at least, the average recovery was between $3 and $4 a ton.

name: Morgan mine (1100 'flat vein')
quote: This ore in 1924—1925 was yielding an average of $4.50 to $5 a ton and these veins were then furnishing about one-third of tonnage milled.

name: Melones mine (Melones Mining Company period)
quote: So far as. can be learned, the average recovery for an entire year only once exceeded $2.70 a ton and during only a few years was it over $2 a ton. The total production was about $4,500,000 under Melones Mining Company.

name: Demarest mine
quote: The total production for these years is claimed to have been about $40,000 from ore that averaged slightly over $8 a ton.

name: Gold Cliff mine (upper crushed zone)
quote: The entire mass in this crushed zone is said to have averaged $2 to $2.50 a ton, and was cheaply mined and yielded a profit.

name: Gwin mine
quote: The ore evidently ranged in average value from $3 to $7 a ton in free gold and the best of it appears to have come from depths of 1300 to 1400 feet, where the vein reached a thickness of 20 to 30 feet. The average jueld in 1882 was reported at $6 a ton and cost of mining and milling $3 a ton.

name: Gwin mine (1897-1900)
quote: The following is a partial record of the results of this period of operation: Januarv, 1897, to April 1, 1900—171,748 tons vielded $702,003.81; April 1,' 1900, to April 1, 1901—99,211 tons vielded $419,421.48; dividends 1897-November 30, 1901, $266,000.

name: Maltman mine
quote: By 1903, the shaft had been sunk to the 200-ft. level and in that year the last production of record was made, reported as averaging $5 a ton.

name: Sultana mine
quote: In the 1860 's a 10-stamp mill and much other equipment was operated and the mine was opened to a depth of 300 ft. It was said the ore yielded from $6 to $26 a ton.

name: Tollgate prospect
quote: Less than 100 tons milled is reported to have assayed well and to have yielded about $4 a ton in free gold, with an unknown amount in the .sulphides.

name: Utica mine (later operations)
quote: In the later operations the ore from the Utica averaged $3.60 or less per ton. The working cost in 1913 was $2.15 a ton.

name: Alabama mine
quote: The estimated production was $150,000. The last reported production was in 1909, when 2302 tons yielded $3,765 gold and $52 silver.

name: Alameda mine (east vein)
quote: No information about assay values is to be had the mine has been idle over 20 years. The east vein is reported to have milled $20 a ton.

name: App mine (1859-1866)
quote: From May 1, 1859, to September 1, 1866, a total of 8027 tons of ore yielded $124,575 or $15.52 a ton at an average mining and milling cost of $7.47 a ton. This was between the surface and 350 ft. deep.

name: App and Heslep mines (combined, 1906-1912)
quote: From a total recorded production of $1,617,308 from 1888 to 1917 which can be credited to the App and Heslep with fair certainty, a weighted average recovery of $3.88 a ton is obtained for the period 1906 to 1912, inclusive, when 353,600 tons of ore was crushed.

name: Atlas mine (picked ore)
tonnage: a few hundred tons of picked ore
quote: Later a shaft was sunk 375 ft. and from 1913 to 1916 a few hundred tons of picked ore was produced, yielding from $13 to $55 a ton.

name: Arbona mine
quote: Two brief periods of activity are recorded in 1900 and 1901 when about $6,000 was produced, and again in 1908-1909 when about 3000 tons crushed gave a return of $1.92 a ton.

name: Dutch mine (Dutch-Sweeney period)
quote: During this period the gross production was $1,126,689 and yield varied from $2.20 to $4.40 a ton. Concentrate varied in value from $35 to $42 a ton and formed from 3^% to 5% of ore.

name: Eagle Shawmut mine (weighted averages)
quote: From 1902 to 1910 the weighted average recovered value of ore was $2.20 a ton. From 1911 to 1926, inclusive, the weighted average recovered value per ton was $3.90.

name: Harvard mine (Trio and Mooney claims)
quote: The Trio and Mooney claims, when worked in early days, produced ore containing about $4.75 a ton in gold and most of the ore has been medium- or low-grade, although one narrow vein at the serpentine contact in the south workings produced a small tonnage of very rich ore.

name: Heslep mine
quote: In 1873, at a depth of 270 ft., the ore-shoot in the Heslep vein was reported 10 ft. wide, 165 ft. long and milling value $9.75 a ton, including the concentrate which formed 2^% of the ore and assayed $40 a ton.

name: Heslep mine (Whitford vein remnant)
quote: The remnant worked by Keyes yielded an average of over $7 a ton in gold and silver. The amount of silver in this ore was notably higher than in other veins of the district, at times exceeding in weight the gold content.

name: Jumper mine
quote: The period of hea^aest production was from 1896 to 1904. For the years when tonnage figures are available, the average value recovered was $5.25 a ton.

name: Jumper mine (July 1899 mill run)
quote: In July, 1899, when operations were in the zone from 300-ft. probably to 600-ft. level, the mill ran 23 days, and crushed 3500 tons of ore which yielded $27,500 or $7.85 a ton.

name: Golden Rule mine (east vein)
quote: During the same month, 810 tons from the Golden Rule east vein yielded $4,350 or $5.37 a ton, whereas 700 tons from the middle vein returned only $1,110 or $1.58 a ton.

name: Rawhide mine
quote: In 1867, this mine had a shaft 280 ft. deep, and a drift 80 ft. long had been run, showing a reported width of 12 ft. of ore ranging in value from $7 to $44 a ton.

name: Mariposa mine (1870 milling)
quote: Soon after, the grade of ore fell off to $10 or $11 a ton and the mine was closed in October, 1870, after three months milling with 25 stamps gave an average of $9.98 a ton, scarcely enough, it was stated, to pay expenses.

name: Mariposa mine (1900-1915)
quote: Between December 20, 1900, and the end of 1915, the mine produced 112,379 tons which yielded $693,205. Work reached a depth of 1550 ft.

name: Pine Tree and Josephine mines (1860-1863)
quote: From June, 1860, to May, 1863, the output of the Pine Tree and Josephine was $350,000 from 45,000 tons of ore.

name: Pine Tree and Josephine mines (1934 operations)
quote: Favorable and creditable costs for mining, development and milling were being achieved, and an operating profit was being made on ore yielding from 0.2 to 0.3 ounce of gold per ton.

name: Princeton mine (1900-1915)
quote: Soon after, the Princeton resumed its position as the best producer in the county, yielding $1,228,273.56 from 350,329 tons of ore between 1900 and 1915, nearlv all prior to 1911.

name: Princeton mine (600-1,000-foot levels)
quote: The new operators, under the management of John H. Mackenzie, sank deeper and found "long and wide bodies of good ore $5 and $4.50 a ton, between 600 and 1000 ft. levels," according to Mackenzie.
